origin: D-22a: surface that the Flutter plugin already exposes between its Dart layer and the native Android SDK; the React Native, Capacitor/Cordova/Ionic and .NET MAUI layers (D-22a..c) replicate this set and add no logic of their own
notes: Any other error code is the stable `code` of an SDK error (SentomaruError, EnrollmentError) forwarded as is.

A `bytes` value (sign.body in, sealedLoad out) crosses a text channel as canonical RFC 4648 section 4 Base64: standard alphabet, padding, no whitespace, no non-zero trailing bits. A reader refuses any other text as ChannelError, or IllegalArgumentException from the Kotlin adapters on the way in (shared sdk/hybrid-core CanonicalBase64; vectors: hybrid-bridge-v1-vectors.json, bytes and bytesRejected).
A hybrid layer adds no method, no default and no retry: a method missing here is a change of this contract first.
iOS of each layer only after the layer's Android gate (D-22, D-09/D-10 are done).

Security rule (revisor A, rodada 2, médio A): `allowedHosts`, `enrollmentUrl` and `renewalUrl` come from this channel, i.e. from the app's JavaScript/XAML/Blazor side, which on Capacitor, Cordova and a WebView-hosted .NET MAUI page is not necessarily the app's own code (injected or compromised page content can call `initialize`). Every dispatcher implementing this contract locks these three fields on the first accepted `initialize` for the life of the bridge instance: a later `initialize` is accepted only when its `allowedHosts` is a subset of the locked set (the list may only shrink, never grow) and its `enrollmentUrl`/`renewalUrl` are identical to the locked ones (including staying absent, for `renewalUrl`); anything else is `ConfigurationError`, refused before any client is built. The .NET MAUI/Xamarin layer has no native dispatcher of its own in this repository (`INativeSentomaru.CallAsync`'s real implementation - binding/JNI - is a separate, untested-here layer written outside Sentomaru.Hybrid, per that project's own file comment); `Sentomaru.Hybrid.LockingNativeSentomaru` wraps whatever `INativeSentomaru` that adapter provides and enforces this exact rule in front of it, so the .NET side applies the rule even though its native adapter is not shipped from here.

Detach rule (revisor A, rodada 2, baixo E): detaching a bridge (the host went away) refuses any call not yet started and drops the reply of any call still in flight at that moment, but does not stop a call already past that point from finishing - there is no cancellation token threaded through the native SDKs, so an enroll/sign already on the wire runs to completion (an App Attest/Keystore key it spends is spent once, not wasted a second time by a caller that believes it got no answer and retries) and its answer is simply never delivered. Proven on iOS (`HybridBridge`'s `isDetached` guard before touching the client, and again at the moment a reply would be sent; `HybridBridgeTests.testEnrollInFlightWhenDetachFiresCompletesButItsReplyIsDiscarded`) and the same way in Android's `SentomaruBridge` (the `isDetached`-equivalent check before touching `native`, and the queued-call refusal `SealedReaderTest`'s own comment already names as untestable here: `onMethodCall` posts every reply through a real `Looper`, which the JVM test stub no-ops). Not verified for the RN/Capacitor/Cordova Android native modules specifically: they sit on top of the same `SentomaruBridge`, but whether a late reply reaching their own framework (not Flutter's channel, which is the one actually confirmed to drop it) is itself harmless is each module's own thing to confirm before relying on this.
